🇲🇽🎨 "Education transforms people's lives, but above all it transforms the life of nations. When there is education, peace is built. When there is education, a future is built." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Suchiapa, Chiapas Handing out Gertrudis Bocanegra university scholarship cards at the Universidad Politécnica de Chiapas, she asked students whether education is only for personal benefit "or to put it also at the service of others." "Always think that this school was made by the people of Mexico," and the scholarship is given "by the people of Chiapas and the people of Mexico." What they do with it is up to them: "whether you dedicate yourselves exclusively to your own person, or build a different future." Student Sofía Castañeda, who travels about two hours each way to class, said what often decides whether students keep studying "is whether we have the bus fare or not."

🇲🇽🎨 "In that Constitution it was said, from back then, that the sovereignty of our homeland did not lie in a few, but resided in the people of Mexico." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Suchiapa, Chiapas Speaking to engineering students in Suchiapa on November 7, she contrasted Mexico's independence with the rest of Latin America, where it was led by criollo officers of the viceroyalty's army who wanted a country "for themselves." In Mexico it was led by a village priest, Hidalgo, who cried out for independence on September 16 and soon after called for the abolition of slavery, and by his disciple Morelos, who took up the fight after Hidalgo was executed and wrote the Apatzingán Constitution, the basis of the 1917 Constitution: the same education "for the son of the hacendado as for the son of the peon," and "moderate indigence and opulence."
banner: "NO COUNTRY IN THE WORLD LIKE OURS"

🇲🇽✊ "This is the Mexico you got to live in. Be part of history. Don't stay away. Don't watch it go by from your window. Be part of this enormous transformation our country is living. And if you see an injustice, raise your voice, in whatever way you decide." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Suchiapa, Chiapas Closing the scholarship event, she ran through the heroines and heroes "unique in the history of the world": Josefa Ortiz Téllez Girón ("because women don't belong to anyone, we don't belong to the husband we marry"), and Leona Vicario, who answered a conservador who said she joined independence only to follow her husband: "We women love our family, we love our children, but we have the right and the obligation to fight for our homeland." Benito Juárez, Villa, Zapata, Madero, and Chiapas's own Belisario Domínguez, "who raised his voice to say long live freedom of expression." "Like Mexico, there is no other."
banner: "IF YOU SEE AN INJUSTICE, RAISE YOUR VOICE"

text: 🇲🇽🎨 "I have always thought, since I studied physics and then engineering, that engineering is for transforming the world, the same as politics. Good politics is the one we do to transform people's lives, to generate well-being, to generate justice." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Suchiapa, Chiapas She told engineering students that President Lázaro Cárdenas founded the Instituto Politécnico Nacional with the motto "technology in the service of the homeland." Showing a picture of the Rizo de Oro bridge she had opened that morning, designed and built by Mexican engineers, she said it is "not only a marvelous technical advance, it is not only very beautiful, it is also social justice," because people who crossed by raft in one or two hours will now cross in five minutes. "That is Mexican engineering. That is you." The Universidad Politécnica de Chiapas has 3,234 students in 10 engineering programs.
banner: "TECHNOLOGY IN THE SERVICE OF THE HOMELAND"

text: 🇲🇽🎨 "In the 60s they called young people troublemakers. Then in the 90s, during the neoliberal period, they called them ninis. From 2006 to 2018 they called them sicarios. Today all the young people of the country are becarios, because that is where they should be, in the schools." — Mario Delgado, Secretary of Public Education, Suchiapa, Chiapas "Ninis": neither studying nor working. "Sicarios": hitmen. "Becarios": scholarship holders. Delgado said governments stopped building high schools and universities even as Mexico was about to have the most young people in its history. In the last 30 years, 20 technological high schools were built; in just 2 years, Sheinbaum is building more than double that. The Tlalpan mansion of former police chief Arturo "El Negro" Durazo, with a heliport and a greyhound track, "a monument to corruption," will become a Rosario Castellanos national university campus.

🇲🇽✊ "Where does that money come from? How is it that the government can now support people and before it couldn't? Because now taxes are collected from those who must pay them, and now there is no robbing." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, La Concordia, Chiapas "Before, there were no scholarships for girls, boys, young people. At most a few for a select few. The vote was requested in exchange for support. Not now. Now it is universal." In Chiapas every public school student, from primary through university, now has a scholarship. The universal pension for older adults, begun in 2019, and the pension for people with disabilities are constitutional rights, and the pension must rise above inflation every year. More than 400,000 farmers receive Sembrando Vida. "That is the Fourth Transformation of public life."
